strongest_angle: Tracing how core artificial intelligence concepts like artificial neurons, backpropagation, and learning machines were conceptualized decades before the modern hardware and computing power required to run them actually existed.

key_facts.fact: In 1943, Warren S. McCulloch and Walter Pitts published 'A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity' in the Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics, establishing the earliest artificial neurons.
The field of Artificial Intelligence was officially born and named in 1956 at a workshop organized by John McCarthy at the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence.
According to Epoch AI's estimates, GPT-6 Astra used about 10^21 times as much compute as the 1957 Perceptron.
